title: The geometric stalks of a constructible sheaf of modules are finite
statement: Let $T$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme], $\Lambda$ a finite commutative ring, and $\mathcal F$ a constructible sheaf of $\Lambda$-modules on the small etale site $T_{\Et}$ [def-weil-pbc-etale-constructible-sheaf], an object of $\Mod(T_{\Et},\Lambda)$ [def-weil-pbc-etale-sheaves], [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category]. Then for every geometric point $\bar t:\operatorname{Spec}\Omega\to T$ [def-weil-geometric-point] the stalk $\mathcal F_{\bar t}$ of the underlying abelian sheaf of $\mathcal F$ [def-weil-pbc-geometric-stalks] is a finite set; in particular, with the $\Lambda$-module structure induced by the $\Lambda$-module structures of the groups $\mathcal F(U)$, it is a finitely generated $\Lambda$-module.

source.place: Etale Cohomology, proof of Lemma 095N (lemma-category-constructible-modules, line 12412 ff.): 'every stalk F_x is a finite type Lambda-module'; from Definition 03RU (definition-finite-locally-constant) and Definition 03RW (definition-constructible) with Lemma 03Q1 (lemma-stalk-pullback: stalk of an inverse image)
